pages.title: Packages
pages.content:
Packages

Six seasonal stays: Ski week (7 nights, 6-day pass, from €1,640), Ski weekend (3 nights, 2-day pass, from €690), First tracks (5 nights, pass and 4 ski-school mornings, from €1,280), Hiking week (7 nights, guide 3 days, from €1,120), Hut-to-hut (4 nights, 2 in the chalet and 2 in huts, from €860) and Long summer weekend (3 nights, from €480). Prices are per person in a double room with half board.

pages.title: Lift pass
pages.content:
Lift pass

The ski pass is included with winter stays of three or more nights and waits at reception. The ski area has 64 km of pistes and 14 lifts, with the gondola 90 m from the door. Winter lifts run 08:30–16:30 and summer lifts 09:00–17:00.

pages.title: Rooms
pages.content:
Rooms

Eighteen rooms in four types: Twin (22 m², sleeps 2, 6 rooms), Double balcony (26 m², sleeps 2, 7 rooms), Family (34 m², sleeps 4, 4 rooms) and Loft suite (48 m², sleeps 4, 1 room).

pages.title: Summer
pages.content:
Summer

From 20 June to 20 September the gondola and two chairlifts are included with every stay. Hiking week, Hut-to-hut and the Long summer weekend start at the chalet door.

pages.title: Check dates
pages.content:
Check dates

Email us your dates, the number of guests and the package. We reply within one working day with a held room for 48 hours; a 30% deposit confirms it, and dates can change free of charge up to 30 days before arrival.

pages.title: Contact
pages.content:
Contact

Yukishiro Chalet, 3 Chemin de la Télécabine, Valmont-Haut. Reception 07:00–22:00. Phone +41 00 555 01 18. Email stay@yukishiro-chalet.example.

pages.title: Snow letter
pages.content:
Snow letter

The first snow report, opening dates and summer trail notes, once a month from October to April.

pages.title: The chalet
pages.content:
The chalet

Anna Brenner and Luc Morel opened Yukishiro Chalet in 2009 in her grandparents' guesthouse in Valmont-Haut, with eleven rooms. The drying room came in 2013, summer stays in 2016, the eighteenth room in 2020 and the hut-to-hut package in 2025.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
Privacy

This sample site stores nothing about you. If you email us your dates, we use your message only to reply.

posts.title: How the drying room works overnight
posts.excerpt: An inside look at the heated racks that ready your boots for morning snow.
posts.content:
At 22:00 the boots come in from the snow and go onto the dryers in the ground-floor drying room. Samuel Okafor, who runs the boot room and ski hire, checks every rack before he goes home: warm air moves through each boot, gloves hang above, and skis stand in the racks by the door.

By 07:00 everything is dry and warm. Guests step into their boots, click into skis outside the door and meet the ski school at 08:45. The room has been part of the chalet since 2013, and many guests say it is the reason they come back.

posts.title: Your first day on skis, from the door
posts.excerpt: Practical advice for beginners stepping into bindings right outside reception.
posts.content:
Your first day starts with breakfast at 07:00 and a boot fitting in the drying room. Ingrid Solheim, our head ski instructor, meets beginners outside the chalet door at 08:45, so there is no bus and no walk with skis on your shoulder.

The First tracks package covers five nights, the lift pass and four ski-school mornings. After the lesson you can have soup in the boot room at 12:30, rest, and ride the gondola, which is ninety metres from the door.

posts.title: Hut-to-hut in four days
posts.excerpt: Crossing high cols and staying in mountain huts along our four-night summer route.
posts.content:
The hut-to-hut package runs for four nights: two in the chalet and two in mountain huts. Tomas Novak, our summer mountain guide, briefs the group at 08:30, and the gondola takes you up at 09:00.

The route crosses the Col Blanc and passes the Ridge of Four Huts. You sleep in the huts, eat lunch on the trail and return to the chalet for a sauna at 17:00 and dinner at 19:30.
